groups.text: It is currently 14 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority is seeking public views on a proposed acquisition in the food manufacturing sector. McCormick & Company intends to acquire the foods business of Unilever Plc, prompting the regulator to open an invitation for comments on how the deal might impact competition within the UK. Interested parties have until August 5th to submit written representations before the formal phase one investigation begins. In separate technical news, PyTorch developers have removed three unreachable CMake branches in a recent update. This cleanup addresses code that could no longer execute, including a condition for CUDA versions older than 12.1 and a duplicate mutual-exclusion check between CUDA and ROCm. The update also removes a skipped flag for unused private fields because it was replaced by a broader unused flag. These changes ensure the software avoids known issues, such as nvcc segfaults on newer CUDA versions.

Tensions have escalated into direct military strikes between the United States and Iran. The U.S. reports that it struck Iranian military command centers, missile launch sites, and air defense systems during overnight operations. In response, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim they hit U.S. military targets across several countries. According to state news agency IRNA, these attacks targeted two air defense systems and a radar installation at two separate U.S. outposts in Bahrain, as well as satellite reception systems, radars, and missile defense systems in Kuwait. The Guards also reported targeting Amazon infrastructure in Bahrain and a U.S. military site in Jordan. Iranian officials warned that this radar sweep is a precursor to more decisive waves of missile and drone attacks.

In Britain, new Prime Minister Andy Burnham is cutting taxes on household electricity bills by removing VAT starting October 1. Downing Street says this will shave roughly 45 pounds off the yearly price cap to give millions of households breathing space this winter. To fund the cut, Burnham is cancelling a Digital ID program that would have cost 1.8 billion pounds over three years. While Britain pivots on digital identity, the Trump administration is pushing a different digital agenda at the United Nations. Washington is circulating a text on freedom of expression to protect Big Tech from European regulations like the DSA and DMA. This contrasts with the reality in authoritarian states where the internet is used as a weapon. In Iran, experts describe the worst internet shutdown in history, leaving activists to rely on LoRa radio technology to communicate via encrypted data packets when the state pulls the plug.

New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is attempting to reposition the country, but he inherits a heavy burden of problems from his predecessor, Keir Starmer. He faces immediate economic constraints and broken public services that cannot be repaired overnight. To deliver quick results for the public, Burnham has signaled plans for tax relief, capped bus fares, and lower energy bills. However, this transition creates a political opening for Nigel Farage. Farage argues that because Burnham was not on the ballot during the 2024 general election, he lacks the democratic legitimacy to lead the government for three years. This tension suggests that any significant shift away from Starmer's original course could trigger demands from Reform UK supporters for new elections. For Burnham, these pressures mean his success depends as much on how he communicates his policies as the policies themselves.

The United States, Russia, and China are competing for dominance over the future of civilian nuclear reactors in Africa. The International Atomic Energy Agency predicts that nuclear capacity across the continent could increase tenfold by 2050 as nations seek to power industrialization and resolve energy deficits. In a different sector of the African economy, Egyptian logistics startup Mylerz has raised more than two million dollars in debt and equity funding. Led by Lorax Capital Partners with participation from Fawry, this capital will allow founder Samer Gharaibeh to expand domestic fulfillment infrastructure and last-mile delivery services. Meanwhile, France is moving toward a strict digital age limit for children. Despite reserves from the European Commission, the French government is pushing a law to ban social media access for those under 15. The text was reviewed by a joint committee and is scheduled for a vote today, aiming for implementation by September.

A researcher is seeking new collaborations on machine learning projects with the goal of producing academic papers. Posting to the r/MachineLearning community, the user known as Puzzleheaded-Bat9316 offered their expertise as a potential co-author for upcoming research. Their technical background includes experience working with Graph Neural Networks and Physics-Informed Neural Networks, as well as unsupervised learning. This outreach highlights a drive for peer-to-peer partnership within the ML community to advance theoretical work into published results. While many researchers operate within large institutional frameworks, this request emphasizes the role of independent networking in driving specialized technical discovery. By offering these specific skill sets, the researcher aims to connect with others currently managing projects that require additional deep learning expertise to reach completion.

Tensions are escalating in the Middle East as Iran targets American radars and defense systems. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard announced attacks on U.S. military sites in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. This comes after the U.S. military concluded ten consecutive nights of bombings against the Islamic Republic. Those American strikes focused on maritime targets and military command centers to reduce Iran's ability to attack commercial ships. In response to these operations, the Revolutionary Guard reports that it has stopped two oil tankers traveling through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz, a path Tehran does not recognize. While these military exchanges intensify, diplomatic pressure continues elsewhere in the region. President Trump has received the Lebanese president amid demands for Hezbollah to disarm.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain cloudy with temperatures between 16 and 22 degrees and rain chances up to 15 percent.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 12:00, Weekly Lunch, at 15:00, RAYX Meeting, and at 18:00, Krebs at c-base.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
